messages:
morgan_curation: quick heads up — we're starting bring-up for q4b-6b quant candidate (q8_0 per-channel). before we run the full eval harness we need a fast dedupe + deid sweep on the prompt set. can label ops take a small task to gate near-duplicates and obvious PII?

 eva_ml: yes can do. what's the target sample and the exact dedupe criteria? fuzzy threshold? paraphrase detection?

 morgan_curation: target ~12k prompts (mix of short/long). prefer fuzzy-dedupe at 0.82, token-normalized overlap > 0.9 filter for trivials, plus regex PII pass (emails, SSNs, credit card-like). also flag long ctx > 4096 for reroute.

 jordan_research: for evaluation we need a clean calibration set (2000 examples) that is stratified across intent buckets. let's avoid the usual 'golden' term — calling it "calibration/anchor" set this time. please keep 20% adversarial/edge.

 alex_runtime: FYI quant config: q8_0 + per-channel scaling, KV cache unchanged. on our internal bench we saw 7-9% latency drop for 2k token median, but a small drop in safety/temperature sensitive prompts — worth checking.

 morgan_curation: noted. eva — can you add a label column "safety_risk" so we can tag severity 0/1/2? that'll help filter when we run BLEURT/BERTScore comparisons.

 eva_ml: yep. I'll create a task for the labelers. approximate turnaround 48h if we batch into 4 labeler buckets.

 labelops_bot: labelops: new task LP-4321 created by <@morgan_curation> — "dedupe + deid sweep for q4b-6b bring-up". 12k items, due 2023-11-27. assigned: @eva_ml, @labelops_lead.

 sam_sre: quick question — if we reroute long ctx to baseline large model, what's the fallback policy? we need to make sure latency SLA doesn't spike.

 alex_runtime: fallback = baseline-8b (cpu-backed for long ctx) with circuit breaker at 2% errors. routing table updated in canary; will add metric alerts for 95p latency.

 jordan_research: eval plan sketch: run automated metrics (BLEURT, BERTScore, ROUGE-L) + pairwise head-to-head against current hosted-model. sample size 2k calibration + 1k stratified holdouts. if BLEURT delta > 0.03 or a manual severity > 1 for >1% examples, block rollout.

 morgan_curation: good. also include a small human A/B of 200 examples for safety regression triage. labelers should mark examples that are "changed intent" vs "quality drop".

 eva_ml: creating labeling buckets now. one question: for dedupe, do we prefer exact fingerprint or tokenizer-normalized hash?

 morgan_curation: use tokenizer-normalized fingerprint (v2) first pass, then fuzzy-dedupe for paraphrases. keep provenance list for any removed sample. we may want to restore some for the calibration anchor.

 jordan_research: reminder to add the quantization smoke tests to the CI job: ./ci/quant_smoke.sh --model q4b-6b --metrics bleurt,bertscore --sample-file s3://redwood/curation/anchor/2023-11/sample_2k.ndjson

 alex_runtime: added smoke job. also instrument token-level latency breakdown in traces so we can see if KV cache misses spike after quantization.

 eva_ml: labelops flagged ~600 near-duplicates (above 0.92) and ~120 PII hits. pushing a review diff to s3://redwood/curation/reviews/q4b-dedupe-169845.

 morgan_curation: thanks. I'll review the PII hits tomorrow morning and confirm which to redact vs remove.

 sam_sre: small nit — please include request-id header in eval runs so we can correlate with infra traces.

 jordan_research: agreed. final checklist before eval run: 1) dedupe+deid pass done 2) calibration anchor assembled (2k) 3) quant smoke CI passed 4) latency/trace instrumentation on 5) human A/B ready. if all green we run full benchmark tomorrow.

 morgan_curation: sounds good — locking schedule. tagging folks: @eva_ml @alex_runtime @jordan_research @sam_sre. :thumbsup:
